title: Private Credit Cracks, The AI "Boogeyman" & Why Crypto is for Boomers | The Real Eisman Playbook
summary: Eisman, Glenn Schorr and Dwight Collins distinguish private-credit losses from fundraising pressure, debate software disruption and favor durable payments networks. The senior-debt cushion argument is conditionally valid, but current equity valuations and refinancing capacity remain unverified. Later Blue Owl filings show meaningful repayments, worsening residual credit metrics and continued parent fundraising. The dialogue reverses the public/private Blue Owl merger entities. Visa operating resilience is supported, while permanent immunity, price-causality and cross-asset incompatibility claims are overstated.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Glenn Schorr handles private markets and credit; Dwight Collins covers investor sentiment, brokers, payments and SoFi. Turn-taking inferred from named prompts. Host closing explicitly adopts selected points; other guest forecasts remain separate.
framework_points: Separate manager equity, fund liquidity, loan credit and sponsor equity.
Check realizable enterprise value and refinancing, not just original equity contribution.
Challenge AI displacement by examining customer integration and workflow.
Use credit spreads as a comparison signal, not proof that unrelated equities must be mispriced.
tools_and_charts: Blue Owl BDC merger and asset-sale waterfall
transcript_cautions: Public and private entities are reversed in the merger discussion; filing resolves the error.
Recording predates publication: last week references February Blue Owl transaction.
CQS insurer name is uncertain ASR, likely Kuvare.
Guest loan-to-value near 35% becomes about 25% debt in host closing; neither treated as verified industry aggregate.

claims.claim: Sponsor equity is junior to senior debt, so enterprise-value losses first consume equity before impairing the lender under a simple capital stack.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated equity first loss proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Assume one senior debt claim D, junior equity, no priming liabilities or bankruptcy costs, and realizable asset value V. Debt recovers min(D,V), equity max(V-D,0). Equity absorbs falling V until V<D. Original equity contribution does not guarantee current realizable value.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.
claims.proof_assumptions: Assume one senior debt claim D, junior equity, no priming liabilities or bankruptcy costs, and realizable asset value V. Debt recovers min(D,V), equity max(V-D,0). Equity absorbs falling V until V<D. Original equity contribution does not guarantee current realizable value.

claims.test: Establish whether the stated gold equity incompatibility proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Assume equity value rises with expected earnings or lower discount rates and gold demand also rises with lower real yields or risk hedging. Both can increase simultaneously without violating an accounting or pricing identity. Negative correlation is not required; this is a deductive counterexample to should-not coexist, not a historical return calculation.
claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: A SoFi 2025-1 securitization breached a roughly 2.6% cumulative net-loss trigger, redirecting cash to senior holders and warning of credit deterioration.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated sofi cnl trigger proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Inspected original deal identifies partner-loan collateral, but trustee loss reports and exact waterfall breach were not inspected. Do not treat originator branding as proof SoFi holds all affected credit exposure.

evidence.title: SoFi SCLP 2025-1 closing announcement
evidence.finding: SCLP 2025-1 was a co-contributor deal primarily involving collateral previously placed with loan-platform partners. Notes $697.6m. SoFi Bank is a nationally chartered bank; exposure cannot be inferred solely from loan origination branding.

claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: A cumulative-loss trigger can redirect subordinate cash to protect senior securitization investors.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish whether the stated abs trigger waterfall proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Assume an enforceable waterfall requires cash otherwise distributable to junior interests to repay senior principal after threshold breach. The redirection increases senior principal repayment by that cash amount. It does not imply all servicing payments cease or every tranche loses money.

claims.claim: Small credit frays after a prolonged benign cycle may prompt allocators to favor quality and new investments over old loan or private-equity books.
claims.speaker: Glenn Schorr
claims.test: Establish whether the stated flight to quality flows proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: Narrative about allocation incentives; requires fund vintages, flows and realized losses rather than inferring a full crisis from isolated events.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence is insufficient to establish or refute this proposition as stated.
